item.title: Omurice at Urawa Retro Cafes: A Nostalgic Comfort Food Trail — Guide
item.description: Urawa’s cluster of old-fashioned kissaten (retro cafes) has made the neighbourhood a low-key pilgrimage site for fans of omurice — a soft, gently cooked omelette wrapped over ketchup-seasoned fried rice, a beloved Japanese comfort food dish with Western-influenced origins. These cafes, many decorated in a warm, unchanged 1970s-80s aesthetic of wood panelling and vintage furniture, serve the dish alongside strong drip coffee, offering an unhurried, nostalgic dining experience distinct from Tokyo’s trendier cafe scene.

item.title: Saitama Unagi: Grilled Eel Over Rice, a Landlocked Speciality — Guide
item.description: Grilled eel over rice (unaju or unadon) is a beloved Saitama speciality, a somewhat unexpected tradition for a landlocked prefecture that developed thanks to the abundant rivers historically stocked with freshwater eel and the region’s role supplying Edo (old Tokyo) with food. Specialist unagi restaurants, some family-run for generations, prepare the eel with a meticulous process of steaming and charcoal-grilling with a sweet-savoury glaze, resulting in a dish that’s crisp outside and meltingly tender within.
